question: What does the H-Net pooling ablation suggest about fixed-width chunking?
answer: The H-Net pooling ablation suggests that fixed-width chunking is not effective, as the H-Net (pool) variant, which utilizes fixed-width chunking, performs much worse than other H-Net variants [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 12, §3.1 Language Modeling]. This outcome reinforces the inherent limitation of content-agnostic fixed-size chunking, which creates arbitrary separations that can split meaningful semantic units, thereby limiting model expressivity [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 32].
